articles.title: Javed Akhtar hits back at troll criticising him for praising Jawaharlal Nehru: 'Being criticised by someone who is a nobody and will die a nobody'
articles.summary: Lyricist and screenwriter Javed Akhtar recently looked back on an encounter with India's first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, which took place on the
articles.body: Lyricist and screenwriter Javed Akhtar recently looked back on an encounter with India's first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, which took place on the latter's birthday in 1963. However, his nostalgic post on X soon sparked a disagreement with a social media user, who criticised his remarks. Akhtar did not hold back while responding to the comment, delivering a sharp retort.Taking to X on November 14, Akhtar recalled attending Nehru's birthday celebrations at Teen Murti Bhavan when he was just 18. Sharing details of the memorable meeting, he wrote, "#14th November 1963 . I was 18 years old when I had the fortune of going to #Teen Murti to attend #Nehru ji's birthday and had the unforgettable moment of shaking his hand . Who knew it was last birthday ? It was my 2nd and last meeting with him. At the age of 13, I had taken his autograph which I still cherish as a treasure."His post, however, drew a critical response from one X user, who took a dig at both the lyricist and the former Prime Minister, commenting, "A mediocre writer loftily praising mediocre PM."Akhtar responded with an equally pointed remark, hitting back at the user with, "..and being criticized by some one who is a no body and die a no body . Fantasizing some such mediocrity for himself."Javed Akhtar is among India's most celebrated screenwriters, lyricists and poets, and is also known for his political activism. He rose to prominence as one half of the legendary Salim-Javed screenwriting duo, alongside Salim Khan. The pair transformed the landscape of Hindi cinema during the 1970s and 1980s with blockbuster films such as 'Sholay', 'Deewaar', 'Zanjeer' and 'Don'. Their success also helped establish screenwriters as prominent figures in the film industry.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Artistic confluence displayed: Chaturth exhibition showcases works of four artists; each presents unique perspectives and experiences
articles.summary: This November, four prominent artists bring alive countless stories on canvas An at gallery is showcasing the works of four leading artists in Chandigarh.
articles.body: This November, four prominent artists bring alive countless stories on canvasAn at gallery is showcasing the works of four leading artists in Chandigarh. City based Pardeep Singh and Gaurvi Sharma and Hyderabad based Bolgum Sai Aditya and Manas Bholla form the four square, the ‘Chaturth’, in this showcase of four distinct artistic voices, each offering a unique way of seeing, interpreting, and engaging with the world.“The exhibition of a creative confluence of these four artists and we couldn’t think of a more apt title than Chaturth. Each brings a fresh perspective, sensibility, and artistic expression on a shared ground. Each approaches art through an individual visual language, shaped by personal experiences, observations, and an ongoing exploration of form, material, and meaning,” says the co-founder of the gallery, Gurpreet Jauhar.The exhibition titled Chaturth steers clear of singularity. Instead, it celebrates a diversity of expression and the possibilities that emerge when individual artistic journeys meet within a shared space. Where nature lies at the heart of Pardeep’s works, Gaurvi excavates the complexities of being a woman. If Indian mythology runs strongly in the strokes of Bolgum, it’s human-animal conflicts and ecological resilience that draws Manas to pursue art.“The beauty of art is the co-existence of multiple narratives, engaging and encouraging us to initiate a dialogue, a connection, a conversation beyond the usual,” adds co-founder, Munish Jauhar, who firmly believes that art creates opportunities for these worlds to intersect, resonate, and inspireGet the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Will Ranbir Kapoor's 'Ramayana' recover its Rs 4000 crore budget? Lara Dutta who plays Kaikeye says, 'I think it will far surpass it'
articles.summary: Nitesh Tiwari's 'Ramayana: Part 1' continues to enjoy a phenomenal run at the box office, having crossed the Rs 1,400 crore mark worldwide and Rs 750
articles.body: Nitesh Tiwari's 'Ramayana: Part 1' continues to enjoy a phenomenal run at the box office, having crossed the Rs 1,400 crore mark worldwide and Rs 750 crore in India. Amid the film's impressive performance, questions have been raised about whether the two-part saga, backed by Namit Malhotra and reportedly mounted on a staggering Rs 4,000 crore budget, will be able to recover its massive investment. Actor Lara Dutta, who plays Queen Kaikeyi in the film, has now shared her thoughts on the possibility of achieving that milestone.In an exclusive conversation with NDTV, Lara expressed confidence that the film would not only recover its costs but also surpass expectations. She said, "We're finally standing, literally, as giants alongside the best of the best films that have been made anywhere else in the world. And it takes so much internal strength to drown out the naysayers and the doubters, and then just keep focused on your vision and keep going. So, will the film make its money back or recover it? I am pretty, pretty, pretty certain it will, not just through the box office, but with whatever Namit has decided to do with it. I don't think it will just recover. I think it will far surpass it."The actor also praised the scale of the ambitious project and Malhotra's conviction in bringing it to life. Speaking about the pride she felt watching the film at its premiere, she added, "I say it is tremendous. It takes a tremendous amount of bravery to put your money where your mouth is, literally, and to create something like this. Today, apart from being an actor in this film, I am so proud to be an Indian. When I saw that film at the premiere, it made me so proud. And I think that's the one sentiment Indians across the world feel today. When they're going into a cinema and stepping out after watching this film, they're all saying that."Lara further pointed out that the audience response to the first instalment has already created anticipation for its sequel. According to her, viewers walking out of theatres are eager to see what happens next, which in itself speaks volumes about the film's impact.In 'Ramayana: Part 1', Lara portrays Kaikeyi, the third wife of King Dasharatha and mother of Bharata. Her character plays a pivotal role in the epic, invoking two boons promised to her by Dasharatha. Through the first, she demands that Bharata be crowned the king of Ayodhya, while the second ensures Rama's exile to the forest for 14 years, with Sita and Lakshman accompanying him.Kaikeyi's decisions are influenced in part by Manthara, her loyal maid, who sows doubts about Rama's intentions and makes her anxious about Bharata's future. Often remembered as the antagonist responsible for Rama's exile, Kaikeyi is also one of the most misunderstood figures in the epic. Her actions stem from a complex mix of vulnerabilities, internal conflict, guilt and remorse, as she unknowingly sets a larger divine prophecy into motion.Lara also offered insights into Kaikeyi's life before the events of the Ramayana, highlighting her upbringing as a warrior princess in the kingdom of Kekaya. Sharing details about her character's background, she said, "Kaikeyi came from the kingdom of Kekaya and Kekaya was known for its horses. It was highland, you know, sort of country, rocky, mountainous country, and they were known for their mountain horses."Elaborating on Kaikeyi's abilities and childhood, the actor added, "She was an excellent horse rider. She was an excellent archer. She grew up a girl among boys. You know, she had only brothers."Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more.
